messages:
alex_k: Hey, heads up — CI started failing in nightly builds. GHA runner shows 403 when fetching repo secrets from the secrets-store proxy. Started ~02:10 UTC this morning.

maya_s: Ugh, saw that on a couple runs. Error looks like an auth/scopes problem. Any logs?

alex_k: Paste of the failed request from runner-proxy: 
```
Request POST /v1/projects/billing-proj/secrets: 403 Forbidden
{"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"serviceAccount:ci-builder@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com missing roles/storage.objectViewer for project billing-proj"}
```

sam_irwin: Two rapid guesses: 1) signed JWT audience changed (runner expects one audience but GCP validating another), 2) service account had RBAC trimmed during yesterday's least-privilege sweep.

alex_k: We didn't change RBAC on billing-proj recently per the audit, but we did rotate a key for ci-builder SA yesterday. Runner-proxy caches signed JWTs for N seconds by default. If cache TTL > key rotation window, signed token could be stale vs new key metadata?

maya_s: Cache TTL explanation makes sense. If the runner is reusing a signed token that was created with the old key id (kid) which GCP no longer accepts, validation might fail with insufficient_scope. But usually GCP returns invalid_grant for bad signature. The payload aud/claims matter too.

alex_k: Repro steps from my local:
```
# generate signed JWT (simulating runner-proxy flow)
python sign_jwt.py --sa ci-builder@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com --payload payload.json > out.jwt
# inspect aud
python -c "import jwt,sys; print(jwt.decode(open('out.jwt').read(), options={'verify_signature':False})['aud'])"
```

alex_k: The aud in the signed jwt on failing runs = "https://secrets.internal.redwood/api" but the proxy currently validates against the GCP resource name service account audience (expected: //iam.googleapis.com/projects/...). So mismatch.

sam_irwin: AH — runner-proxy config recently had a refactor to accept both old and new audiences, but the release flagged in the deploy-bot changed the default back to strict mode. deploy-bot, any deploy info?

deploy-bot: deploy job #2541 marked a config change to runner-proxy: set STRICT_AUD_CHECK=true in production during canary on 3790009000. No rollback executed. :information_source:

maya_s: That would turn on strict aud check and reject tokens with custom audience. Some internal pipelines sign JWTs for proxy with custom aud to limit scope — those tokens now fail.

alex_k: Quick mitigation: flip STRICT_AUD_CHECK=false in canary group or adjust runner to sign with the expected GCP audience. Which is less risky?

sam_irwin: Short term: disable strict aud in the canary group so existing tokens accepted. Medium term: update signing library and runner config to produce the canonical aud. Also add integration test asserting aud validation post-deploy.

maya_s: Also add a health check that detects signed-jwt "kid" rotation mismatches: compare the service account public key set against the kid in cached tokens and force refresh if mismatch.

alex_k: I pushed a hotfix to the canary config and restarted proxies in canary. Monitoring shows recent runs now pass. Will propagate to prod after 30m stable window.

ops-bot: Alert suppressed: CI-failure (rule: secrets-proxy-403) acknowledged by alex_k.

sam_irwin: For the permanent fix, can we also lower the cache TTL to something like 5m and add jitter to avoid fanout during rotation? Current TTL = 1h.

alex_k: Yep, lowering TTL and adding jitter is in my TODO. Will also open a follow-up ticket to update docs on what aud runners should use for signing.

maya_s: Thanks — can you paste the exact remediation steps in the ticket so oncall can follow during future rotations?

alex_k: Will do. For the record I ran these commands to verify: 
```
# check active keys for SA
gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=ci-builder@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com --format=json | jq '.[].name'
# decode token to check kid/aud
python -c "import jwt,json; t=open('out.jwt').read(); print(json.dumps(jwt.get_unverified_header(t),indent=2)); print(jwt.decode(t, options={'verify_signature':False}))"
```

maya_s: Great, thanks. Closing on this thread once prod rollout finishes. :thumbsup:

alex_k: FYI ticket: INF-4921 created with notes + remediation steps.

sam_irwin: Nice work catching the aud strictness regression quickly.

alex_k: Cheers — will update when prod is stable.
